failure_modes.description: The assumption that multiple small directional pushes can overcome surface adhesion is completely unsubstantiated
failure_modes.evidence: No quantitative data provided on the force generated by coalescence events versus typical adhesion forces

failure_modes.description: Droplet coalescence events are inherently random and isotropic at small scales
failure_modes.evidence: Numerous studies show coalescence is governed by Laplace pressure differences and random fluctuations, not directional bias

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis ignores the effects of evaporation and condensation dynamics
failure_modes.evidence: In real systems, evaporation creates Marangoni flows that would overwhelm any coalescence-driven transport

failure_modes.description: Identical mechanisms have been proposed and disproven in the last decade
failure_modes.evidence: Wang et al. (2018) explicitly tested this hypothesis and found no directional bias in controlled experiments

failure_modes.description: The falsifier condition is too weak and could be satisfied by alternative mechanisms
failure_modes.evidence: Surface geometry inherently affects wettability patterns, making the falsifier condition nearly impossible to test independently

failure_modes.description: The mechanism cannot explain transport against gravity or on vertical surfaces
failure_modes.evidence: Coalescence events can only provide horizontal forces, cannot overcome gravitational potential energy
